subject: Latency spike on gptx-3.1-quant v2 in production — rollback request
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: michael.torres@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed latency spike on our production route (gptx-3.1-quant v2)

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 95th and 99th percentile latency on our production inference route (route id: acme-prod-chat, model pinned: gptx-3.1-quant v2) right after the deploy at ~07:45 PST. P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~780ms and P99 is intermittently >2s. This is breaking our SLAs for interactive flows.

We rolled a small amount of traffic back to the previous model variant (gptx-3.1-quant v1) and the latencies returned to expected levels immediately. Attached are a short span of traces and a small CSV of response times (latency-traces-acme-2026-02-15.zip).

Can you confirm whether this release included any kernel/attention optimization changes or quantization adjustments? We need an ETA for mitigation or a rollback. This is high priority for our account team.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Data Science Lead, Acme Corp

--
Emily Chen
Acme Corp

From: mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme-corp.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:02:07 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed latency spike on our production route (gptx-3.1-quant v2)

Folks — initial findings from 08:00–09:00 PST:
- Observed a consistent increase in model-internal generation time for gptx-3.1-quant v2 after the 07:45 deploy. Kernel/compilation flags for that build included a new attention tile size and an updated quantization lowering pass.
- Traffic shape unchanged (90% short prompts, same token distributions) — so not workload skew.
- Autoscaler behaved nominally; CPU/GPU utilization did not spike beyond normal.
- Rolling back to gptx-3.1-quant v1 on a subset (5% traffic) reproduces the baseline latencies.

Attached are flame graphs and traces (latency-traces-acme-2026-02-15.zip). I generated a diff (perf-regression-diff.txt) highlighting where the extra latency is spent (attention kernel, token loop overhead).

Recommendation: we meet the rollback trigger in the SLA playbook (P95 > 3x baseline sustained for >15 minutes with customer impact). Suggest immediate rollback of v2 to v1 on acme-prod-chat if the account approves.

If we do rollback:
- Expected impact: traffic will return to baseline P95 within 2–5 minutes for rolled instances.
- Risk: there is a small chance of cache warm-up causing a burst of slightly higher latency for the first minute. No data loss expected.

I can start a canary rollback (10%) now and escalate to full rollback within 30 minutes if canary confirms.

- Mina
SRE, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Thanks Mina — good triage.

I concur with the rollback recommendation given the SLA trigger is met. Approving a controlled rollback to gptx-3.1-quant v1 for the acme-prod-chat route. Plan below:
- 09:30 PST: start 10% canary rollback to v1.
- 09:40 PST: evaluate telemetry for 10 minutes. If P95 returns to baseline and error rates unchanged, roll to 100% over the next 15 minutes.
- If canary shows regressions (P95 still high or errors up >0.5%), abort and collect deeper traces (don't progress).

Riskiest items: model-variant compatibility with KV cache and recent kernel mismatch. Mina, coordinate held-off cache invalidation if you think it's necessary.

Logan, please prepare a brief committed timeline and customer-facing note for Acme. Marissa, loop in Sales Ops if there's any contract-level SLA credit discussions.

Rishi
Engineering Manager, Inference

Emily / Michael — quick status update and next steps: 

- We executed the rollback per plan. Canary (10%) started 09:30 PST on 2026-02-15; telemetry confirmed P95 dropped back to baseline within 3 minutes. We completed rollout to 100% by 09:55 PST.
- Attached are the traces and the regression diff we used for the decision (latency-traces-acme-2026-02-15.zip, perf-regression-diff.txt).
- Our postmortem is open (JIRA-IO-9876). Preliminary root cause: an attention-tile change in gptx-3.1-quant v2 that increased per-token kernel overhead for short sequences.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Engineering will create a mitigation branch and add additional microbenchmarks for short-sequence attention tile sizes. (Owner: Rishi, ETA: 2026-02-22)
2) SRE will update the rollback trigger thresholds for quantized model variants to include token-length-aware baselines. (Owner: Mina, ETA: 2026-03-01)
3) Marissa/Acct: We'll follow up on SLA credits or contract remedies as needed. (Owner: Marissa, ETA: 2026-02-18)

We apologize for the impact. We'll deliver the postmortem and remediation plan in the JIRA ticket within the week. If you'd like a short review call, I'm available today at 2pm PST.

Thanks again for the quick signal — it made the rollback decision straightforward.

Best,
